summary: Restoration and mixed forest commitments aim to expand forest cover by 145 kha by 2032 (the next 10 years), through 110 kha of new afforestation/production forests and 35 kha of rehabilitation; this equals about 60% of Moldova’s current 2,422 km² forest area. The expansion is expected to raise sequestration potential by around 56%. A separate NFERP program supports planting or rehabilitation of over 63.2 kha in 2024–2028, while 1.0 million MDL is earmarked for urban and rural green spaces and proposed centers would provide 85–90 million seedlings annually. Conservation combines a 10% reduction in municipal and industrial water-system losses with halting deforestation and degradation by 2030. Agriculture targets a 20% expansion of organically farmed land, drip irrigation on 133.5 thousand ha of orchards and 135.3 thousand ha of vineyards—about 4.6% each and 9.2% combined of current agricultural area—and at least 40% of subsidies for women-led initiatives.
